tagline: A dredged shortcut across Old Tampa Bay became a scenic highway
intro: State Road 60 crosses Old Tampa Bay on the Courtney Campbell Causeway between Clearwater and Tampa. The ten-mile scenic highway runs at sea level, with a paved walking and cycling trail beside the road for its full length. Florida designated it on May 23, 2005; the state’s scenic-highway program emphasizes its bay views and the causeway habitat that provides food, shelter and breeding space for wildlife.

Before the causeway, the land route between Tampa and Clearwater ran more than 30 miles along the bay’s northern shore through Oldsmar. Dredging-company owner Ben T. Davis proposed a direct crossing and began work in 1927. Construction proceeded when his dredges had no other work, and the Davis Causeway opened in 1934 with a 25-cent toll per car. The federal government acquired the crossing in 1944 as part of the war effort, and ownership then passed to the state of Florida. It received Courtney Campbell’s name in 1948 after his efforts to secure repairs and beautification.

Driving east from Clearwater, pass the state-owned beach at the western end and cross toward Rocky Point and mainland Tampa. Ben T. Davis Municipal Beach lies at the eastern end. Tampa International Airport is about a mile east of Rocky Point.
notice: Palms and mangroves grow along the causeway, with a paved trail beside the road.

moments.title: Courtney Campbell Causeway
moments.text: The causeway’s raised spans let watercraft pass between parts of Old Tampa Bay. A later alteration addressed the water itself: work began in 2018 on a channel through the eastern side to improve water quality north of the road. That project was completed in July 2019. Frontage roads flank the main four-lane highway, interrupted by bridge spans. The paved multi-use trail follows the entire corridor, providing a route for walkers and cyclists across the bay. At the Pinellas County end, the causeway trail connects with the Ream Wilson Clearwater Trail and, through it, the Pinellas Trail.

moments.title: Ben T. Davis Beach
moments.text: The eastern beach carries the name the causeway bore when it opened: Ben T. Davis. Davis owned the dredging company behind the crossing, which opened to cars in 1934. The road was renamed for Courtney Campbell in 1948, while the City of Tampa maintains Ben T. Davis Municipal Beach at the eastern end. The opposite end has another beach, owned by the Florida Department of Transportation.

moments.title: Rocky Point
moments.text: At Rocky Point, the causeway connects the island with mainland Tampa and continues west to Clearwater. The area contains the world headquarters of Shriners International and Rocky Point Golf Course, one of Florida’s oldest courses. The Tampa Automobile Club established the course in 1911, and its first nine holes opened in 1912. The club took the Rocky Point name in 1917. During World War II, the federal government closed it for use as part of Drew Field and built barracks to house prisoners of war. It reopened as a golf course in 1954.
